title: Functions
summary: Write your own commands with def and return.

blocks.text: You have been calling functions like move() and explore() since the first lesson. Now you can make your own with 'def' (short for define):
Defining a function does not run it. It teaches the golem a new word. The body only runs when you call the function by name.

blocks.tip: Define your functions at the top of the program, before the main loop that uses them.

blocks.text: Functions get more useful when they take arguments. The names in the brackets of def are parameters: variables that are filled in by each call.
When you call fight(nearest_enemy()), the nearest enemy is stored in 'enemy' for that call only. Variables created inside a function are local: they disappear when it finishes.
'return' ends the function and hands a value back to whoever called it, just like nearest_enemy() hands back an enemy:
Good functions do one clear job and have a name that says what it is. Your main loop then reads like a plan: if is_hurt(): recall().

blocks.tip: The Inspector shows the call stack: which function is running, and who called it.

challenge.brief: A skeleton patrols the Bone Hall. Write a fight(enemy) function that attacks when the enemy is close and approaches it otherwise, then reach the stairs without breaking.
